thesis: Howard Marks argues that being right too slowly is ineffective and that successful investing depends on buying things well rather than just buying good things, as high prices can lead to significant losses even in great companies. He illustrates this by comparing the 'no price too high' mentality of the Nifty Fifty era and the late 1990s TMT bubble, noting that while the internet changed the world, investors still lost nearly all their money in companies with no profits or revenues because they ignored valuation and due diligence.
